facts.statement: The study compared mice engineered to produce a specific protein in their muscles against standard mice at young and old ages.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Researchers measured changes in gene activity, muscle fiber structure, blood vessel supply, nerve connections, and energy-producing organelles in the leg muscles.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Activating the target protein turned on 574 genes related to energy production and blood flow while turning off genes that cause muscle wasting.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The modified mice had more energy-producing organelles and a higher proportion of endurance-type muscle fibers compared to the standard mice.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The protein activation helped maintain the number of nerve connections to the muscle and reduced the shrinkage of muscle fibers seen in aging.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Older mice with the activated protein showed much less loss of muscle strength compared to older standard mice.
facts.subject: animals
